advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile referencing_commit_diffs (`git show --stat`) with the docstring/prompt claim of 'diffs': either include real diff hunks or rename the concept to 'commit summaries'.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_prefetch.py:311-315: "show", "--stat", "--format=%H%n%s%n", sha
Module docstring line 1: "Pre-fetch declared file_impact contents + referencing-commit diffs"
completion_verifier.md:271: "the file bodies (and any referencing-commit diffs) pre-loaded"
advisory.finding: referencing_commit_diffs runs `git show --stat` (plus subject/hash format), which emits only a per-file change SUMMARY, not the actual diff hunks. The module docstring, the commit message, and the verifier prompt all promise 'referencing-commit diffs', so the verifier is told it has diff content it never receives.
advisory.suggested_fix: Either drop `--stat` (or add `-p`) to include actual diff content, or change all docstrings/prompt text to say 'referencing-commit summaries' rather than 'diffs'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile distinct_fetches recording verbatim search queries with usage_log's stated 'no tool-argument content' privacy contract (record only paths, or update the contract).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:172-173: "Prompts, response text, tool arguments, and tool results are deliberately excluded so the payload is safe for a durable gate-error record."
src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:293: "search_files": ("query", "pattern", "regex")
fetch_target docstring line 286: "no content leak into the run shape" — yet a search query IS free-form model content
advisory.finding: distinct_fetches records the raw `search_files` query string (and read_file paths) verbatim into the durable run-shape record, contradicting usage_log's stated privacy contract that tool arguments are HASHED and never recorded so the payload is 'safe for a durable gate-error record'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] On ceiling-trim, re-append the closing </prefetched_file_contents> tag and reconcile the PRE-LOAD MANIFEST with the files actually retained.
evidence: completion_prefetch.py:233 `trimmed = prefetch_section[:boundary]` cuts before the closing tag at line 196 `f"...</{PREFETCH_TAG}>"`
completion_prefetch.py:236 `result = trimmed + marker` never re-adds the closing tag
Manifest is built once in clamp_and_format (lines 192-195) before any ceiling trimming, so trimmed files remain listed
advisory.finding: fit_within_ceiling, when it truncates, appends a marker but drops the closing </prefetched_file_contents> tag, and the PRE-LOAD MANIFEST still lists files whose bodies were trimmed away — so the manifest overstates what is actually present and the fenced section is left unclosed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (or enforce) that assemble_context's prefetch path is NOT ceiling-bounded, so future callers apply fit_within_ceiling as gate_ops does.
evidence: operations.py:129-131 appends section with no ceiling check
gate_ops.py:154 calls assemble_context with prefetch omitted, then applies fit_within_ceiling separately at line 166
assemble_context docstring (98-103) does not warn that the prefetch path is unbounded by the model ceiling
advisory.finding: assemble_context's built-in prefetch path (prefetch=PrefetchSpec) appends the prefetch section WITHOUT any physical-context-ceiling fit; only gate_ops applies fit_within_ceiling, and it deliberately bypasses assemble_context's prefetch param. A future caller passing prefetch= directly would silently get an unbounded, potentially over-ceiling context.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Skip skeleton_compress for non-source pseudo-bodies (e.g. referencing-commit entries) in clamp_and_format.
evidence: clamp_and_format:179 skeletonizes on `body.count('\n') + 1 > SKELETON_LINE_THRESHOLD` regardless of path type
assemble_prefetch:390-392 adds pseudo-path `referencing-commit {sha}` into bodies
skeleton_compress keeps only def/class/@ lines (line 100-106); a git diff/stat has none, so all lines elide
advisory.finding: skeleton_compress can be applied to a referencing-commit pseudo-body (a git stat summary, not Python). If such a body exceeds SKELETON_LINE_THRESHOLD lines, clamp_and_format skeletonizes it, and since diff/stat lines never match _is_signature_line the whole body collapses to a single 'lines elided; call read_file' marker pointing at pseudo-path 'referencing-commit <sha>' which is not a readable file.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the "referencing-commit diffs" wording (verifier.md and completion_prefetch docstring) with the `git show --stat` output actually produced, or include the real diff.
evidence: completion_verifier.md: "the file bodies (and any referencing-commit diffs) pre-loaded"
completion_prefetch.py docstring: "the diffs of the commits that reference the ticket"
referencing_commit_diffs uses: `"show", "--stat", "--format=%H%n%s%n", sha` — `--stat` yields a file-change summary, not a content diff
advisory.finding: Docs claim referencing-commit "diffs" are prefetched, but the code fetches only `git show --stat` (a changed-file summary with insertion/deletion counts), not the actual diff content. Both the module docstring ("referencing-commit diffs") and completion_verifier.md ("any referencing-commit diffs") mislabel the stat summary as a diff.
scenarios: Verifier is told a body/diff is authoritative but only receives a stat summary, so it may assume it has seen the full change when it has not

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that drives the real `assemble_prefetch` (monkeypatch `_reads.show_ticket` + a tmp repo tree, patch `referencing_commit_diffs`) and asserts the assembled section/manifest, including the empty-result contract.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_prefetch.py:359 `def assemble_prefetch(spec: PrefetchSpec, *, repo_root) -> tuple[str, list[dict]]:`

test at tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_prefetch.py:187-189 monkeypatches `rebar.llm.workflow.completion_prefetch.assemble_prefetch` to `lambda spec, *, repo_root: (section, ...)` — the real function never runs
search of tests/ for `assemble_prefetch` returns only these two monkeypatch sites; ABSENCE: no test drives assemble_prefetch against a real repo_root/ticket
advisory.finding: assemble_prefetch (the feature's IO orchestrator) is never exercised end-to-end: both tests referencing it (test_assemble_context_with_spec_appends_section, test_assemble_context_empty_section_appends_nothing) monkeypatch it away with a lambda. Real-body ranking, _discover_test_globs, the append of referencing-commit diffs into the same budget, and the 'no readable paths -> empty section' contract have no test, so a regression in the orchestration logic would not be caught.
scenarios: A change to rank_paths/_read_body wiring, the diffs-into-budget append (completion_prefetch.py:388-392), or the empty-bodies short-circuit (completion_prefetch.py:394-395) ships green.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for `referencing_commit_diffs` (subprocess.run monkeypatched or a real tmp git repo) covering the happy path, char-cap truncation, and the fail-open on nonzero returncode.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_prefetch.py:284 `def referencing_commit_diffs(ticket_id: str, repo_root) -> dict[str, str]:`
ABSENCE: search of tests/ for `referencing_commit_diffs` and `referencing-commit` returns no test of this module's function
advisory.finding: referencing_commit_diffs has no test despite being new behavior and documented as 'trivially monkeypatchable'. Its git-invocation shape, the returncode!=0 fail-open, the per-commit _COMMIT_DIFF_CHAR_CAP truncation, and the _MAX_REFERENCING_COMMITS bound are all unverified.
scenarios: A commit-diff char cap or the recent-commit limit regresses; a non-fail-open git error path is introduced — none caught.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a completion_precheck test that exercises the real prefetch branch (assert the assembled context carries the section) and one with REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH=0 asserting the base context is used unchanged.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py:160 `if os.environ.get("REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH") == "0":`
src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py:164 `section, _manifest = completion_prefetch.assemble_prefetch(spec, repo_root=ctx.repo_root)` then fit_within_ceiling at :166

tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_child_scope.py:70 `monkeypatch.setattr(operations, "assemble_context", _spy)` — replaces the whole assembler, so lines 160-167 of gate_ops never execute in the suite
ABSENCE: search of tests/ for `REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH` returns no matches
advisory.finding: The gate_ops prefetch wiring is untested: the REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH=0 escape-hatch branch and the assemble_prefetch()+fit_within_ceiling() concatenation on the close path (gate_ops.py:160-167) have no test. The pre-existing completion_precheck tests (test_completion_child_scope.py) monkeypatch operations.assemble_context wholesale, so they bypass the new gate code entirely.
scenarios: A regression breaks the escape hatch (prefetch cannot be disabled) or the fit-and-concatenate wiring (base+fitted) — the A/B baseline mechanism silently stops working; no test fails.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen test_fit_within_ceiling_prefers_block_boundary to assert the trimmed output ends at a block boundary (e.g. contains the retained `--- a.py` header and excludes the dropped `--- b.py` block body).
evidence: tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_prefetch.py:145-147 assert only `len(out) <= 200` and `'truncated to fit context ceiling' in out`
src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_prefetch.py:232 `if boundary > 0:` selects block-boundary trim vs :235 hard-truncate — the test named 'prefers_block_boundary' does not discriminate these branches
advisory.finding: test_fit_within_ceiling_prefers_block_boundary does not actually verify block-boundary trimming: it asserts only len<=200 and that the truncation marker is present, both of which a plain hard-truncate (the else branch) would also satisfy. The distinguishing behavior — that a whole trailing '--- b.py ---' block is cut and the '--- a.py ---' block retained via the `boundary > 0` branch — is not asserted, so a regression collapsing block-aware trimming to hard truncation passes.
scenarios: The block-boundary rfind logic is removed/regressed to always hard-truncate mid-block; this test stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert `'--- a.py (full) ---' in out` and `'--- b.py (full) ---' not in out` (or that `out` before the marker ends exactly at the block boundary).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Route `completion_prefetch._read_body` (and `_discover_test_globs` matches) through `fs_tools._safe_path` + `config.is_denied` so prefetch reads honor the same traversal/deny-list confinement as the verifier's `read_file` tool.
evidence: completion_prefetch.py:329-335: `full = os.path.join(str(repo_root), path)` then `open(full, ...)` with no confinement/deny check

fs_tools.py:24-32 `_safe_path`: `if abs_path != root and not abs_path.startswith(root + os.sep): raise ValueError('path escapes the repository root')` plus `if _is_denied(abs_path, denied)` — the guard the normal read tool applies

config.py:300-306 `denied_paths`: 'Realpaths the agent must never read OR cite: git internals, reconciler state, and the live event store ... so neither can leak internal state' — includes `.git`, `.bridge_state`, `.tickets-tracker`, tracker_dir
pai_tools.py:50-56: verifier `read_file` routes through `_safe_path(root, path, denied)` before opening

leaf.py:160-183 `_validate_json_array` / set_file_impact: file_impact entries validated only as objects with string `path`/`reason` — no traversal or deny-list validation on the path value, so `..`/denied paths are accepted

Taint flow: file_impact path -> `_normalize_impact` -> `ranked` -> `_read_body` open -> `clamp_and_format` -> `<prefetched_file_contents>` appended in operations.assemble_context (operations.py:122-130)
advisory.finding: `completion_prefetch._read_body` reads ticket-declared `file_impact` paths with a raw `open(os.path.join(repo_root, path))`, bypassing the `_safe_path` traversal guard AND the `is_denied` deny-list that the verifier's normal `read_file` tool enforces — so a crafted `file_impact` path (e.g. `../../etc/passwd`, `.git/config`, or a tracker/event-store path) is read and spliced into the verifier's prompt context.
scenarios: A ticket whose declared file_impact path is `../../.ssh/id_rsa`, `.git/config`, or a path into `.tickets-tracker`/event store is passed to the completion gate; `_read_body` reads it and the bytes land in the verifier prompt
Reading a file outside repo_root via `..` traversal even though the sandbox is meant to confine reads to the repo
advisory.suggested_fix: In `_read_body`, resolve the path via `rebar.llm.fs_tools._safe_path(str(repo_root), path, rebar.llm.config.denied_paths(str(repo_root)))` (catching ValueError to skip, preserving fail-open), instead of a bare `os.path.join` + `open`; apply the same deny/confinement filter to `_discover_test_globs` results.
